what_it_does.point: Bars federal Medicaid payments to states for any amount spent on defined 'specified gender transition procedures' for a person under 18 who is enrolled in a state Medicaid plan or a waiver of that plan.
Also bars federal Medicaid payments for the costs of administering a state program that provides those procedures and drugs to people under 18.

Defines 'specified gender transition procedures' as procedures done for the purpose of intentionally changing a person's body — including by disrupting its development, inhibiting its natural functions, or modifying its appearance — so that it no longer corresponds to the person's sex.

Lists covered surgeries under that definition, including castration, sterilization, removal of testicles or ovaries, vasectomy, tubal ligation, hysterectomy, genital construction or removal procedures, throat/voice-box cartilage reduction, mastectomy, and any cosmetic surgery that feminizes or masculinizes facial or other physical features.
Also includes chest implants to create feminine breasts, erection or testicular prostheses, and fat or artificial implants in the buttocks.

Also includes providing medications such as puberty-blocking drugs (gonadotropin-releasing hormone analogues) and doses of testosterone, estrogen, progesterone, or other androgens greater than what a healthy person of the same age and sex would naturally produce.

Creates exceptions, when provided by a health care provider with the consent of a parent or legal guardian, for puberty-blocking drugs used to normalize puberty in a child with early (precocious) puberty.

Creates exceptions for treatment of a medically verifiable genetic disorder of sex development, or abnormal sex chromosome structure, sex hormone production, or hormone action as determined by a physician through genetic or biochemical testing.

Creates exceptions for treating an infection, disease, injury, or disorder caused or worsened by a previously performed listed procedure, and for a physical condition that a physician certifies places the person in imminent danger of death or loss of a major bodily function; procedures done to relieve mental distress are not covered by this exception.

Creates an exception for procedures to restore or reconstruct the body to correspond to the person's sex after one or more of the listed procedures, which may include removal of a pseudo phallus or breast augmentation.

Defines 'sex' as male or female as biologically determined, with 'female' meaning a person whose reproductive system at some point produces, transports, and uses eggs for fertilization, and 'male' meaning a person whose reproductive system at some point produces, transports, and uses sperm — including where this would be the case but for a developmental or genetic anomaly or historical accident.

json.stated_purpose: To amend title XIX of the Social Security Act to prohibit federal Medicaid funding for gender transition procedures for minors.
